public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim is that by late November 2025 no scaled LLM had overcome hallucination, generalization, planning and reasoning as basic limits. In September 2025, OpenAI's own researchers wrote that hallucinations 'persist even in state-of-the-art systems' (e1). In June 2025, Apple researchers found that frontier reasoning models suffer 'complete accuracy collapse' on planning puzzles past a certain complexity (e2). Two days before the post, Sutskever said models 'generalize dramatically worse than people' (e3), which confirms the post's attribution. There was real progress, such as gold-medal-level IMO results in July 2025 (e5) and what ARC Prize later called a profound upgrade in reasoning (e4). But neither source claims these problems were solved, and ARC Prize itself says reasoning systems still have many flaws. The evidence fits the claim that improvements were measurable but the core problems remained unsolved.
limitations: 'Solved' has no stated threshold. Someone who counts IMO gold or big benchmark gains as solving reasoning would read the claim differently.
The hedged diminishing-returns part was not scored.
Some evidence covers particular task families (puzzles, factual recall) rather than the four problem areas as a whole.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No LLM scaling experiment has solved the core problems of hallucination, generalization, planning and reasoning.

statement.excerpt: Each new bigger, more expensive model ekes out measurable improvements, but returns appear to be diminishing (that’s what Sutskever is saying about the Kaplan laws) and none of these experiments has solved core issues around hallucinations, generalization, planning and reasoning, as Sutskever too now recognizes.
statement.document_title: A trillion dollars is a terrible thing to waste

from_speaker: Each new bigger, more expensive model ekes out measurable improvements
none of these experiments has solved core issues
our_interpretation: The scored core is the firm part: that no scaled LLM had, by the post date (2025-11-27), solved hallucination, generalization, planning and reasoning. The 'returns appear to be diminishing' part is hedged ('appear') and is treated as context, not scored separately.

Plain reading of 'solved': the problem has been overcome to the point that it is no longer a basic limitation of frontier models. Steady improvement or strong results on specific benchmarks does not count as 'solved'.
Target period runs from the start of the Kaplan-laws scaling era (2020) to the post date, because the claim covers all such experiments up to then.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence from around late 2025 (lab research, independent evaluations, or leading researchers) showing that state-of-the-art LLMs still had substantial hallucination, generalization, planning or reasoning failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that by late 2025 some scaled LLM had effectively eliminated one or more of these problems, for example hallucination rates near zero on open-ended factual tasks, or robust human-level generalization and planning on new tasks.

evidence.excerpt: Such “hallucinations” persist even in state-of-the-art systems and undermine trust.
evidence.publisher: arXiv (Kalai, Nachum, Vempala, Zhang; OpenAI and Georgia Tech)
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's own researchers say hallucination had not been solved in state-of-the-art models as of September 2025.

evidence.excerpt: we show that frontier LRMs face a complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities. Moreover, they exhibit a counter-intuitive scaling limit
evidence.explanation: Independent tests on planning puzzles such as Tower of Hanoi and Blocks World found that frontier reasoning models fail completely past a certain complexity. That shows reasoning and planning were not solved.

evidence.excerpt: these models somehow just generalize dramatically worse than people. It’s super obvious. That seems like a very fundamental thing.
evidence.explanation: A leading researcher and OpenAI co-founder says generalization remains a basic, unsolved weakness of current models. This also confirms the post's attribution to Sutskever.

evidence.excerpt: As good as AI reasoning systems are, they still exhibit many flaws and inefficiencies necessary for AGI. We still need new ideas
evidence.locator: Section 'AGI Progress & the Future of ARC'
evidence.explanation: The benchmark operator's view of late-2025 frontier systems agrees that reasoning flaws remain. The same post also calls 2025 reasoning systems 'a profound upgrade'. It was published after the post, so it is context only.

evidence.excerpt: Gemini achieved the exact same score as OpenAI, 35/42, and were able to solve the same set of questions - 1 through 5, failing only to answer 6
evidence.explanation: Counterevidence on the size of progress: LLM-based systems reached gold-medal level at the 2025 IMO. This is major reasoning progress on one hard task, but it does not show reasoning was solved in general.
